did_you_know.text: Did you know? Samuel anointed Saul with oil and proclaimed him as the one the LORD had appointed as ruler over His inheritance—Israel.
Did you know? Saul’s first sign was meeting two men near Rachel’s tomb, who would tell him that the donkeys had been found and that his father was now worried about him.
Did you know? In the second sign, Saul met three men going up to Bethel: one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and the third carrying a skin of wine.
Did you know? Two of the three men gave Saul two loaves of bread, and he accepted them from them—as part of the signs Samuel had given him.
Did you know? Near Gibeah of God, Saul met a company of prophets, with a harp, tambourine, flute, and lyre being played before them as they prophesied.
Did you know? Samuel told Saul that the Spirit of the LORD would come powerfully upon him, that he would prophesy with the prophets, and that he would become a different man.
Did you know? When Saul turned to leave Samuel, God gave him a different heart, and all the signs Samuel had foretold came to pass that day.
Did you know? When people who knew Saul saw him prophesying with the prophets, they were astonished, and the saying arose: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
Did you know? When the people looked for Saul after he had been chosen by lot, it turned out that he was hiding among the baggage.
Did you know? After Saul was made king, Samuel wrote the regulations of kingship in a book and placed it before the LORD. Then Samuel sent all the people home, each to his own house.
